content: 1. Trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole is prescribed as 1-2 double-strength (DS) tablets orally every 12-24 hours or intravenously at a dose of 8-20 mg TMP/kg/day divided every 6-12 hours for acute exacerbations of chronic bronchitis caused by susceptible strains of Streptococcus pneumoniae or Haemophilus influenzae. For DS tablets, the recommended dose is 1 tablet orally every 12 hours for 10-14 days. 2. For documented Pneumocystis jiroveci pneumonia (PCP) or prophylaxis against PCP in immunosuppressed individuals, the recommended dose is 20 mg TMP/kg/day intravenously divided every 6 hours. 3. For enteritis caused by susceptible strains of Shigella flexneri and Shigella sonnei, the recommended dose is 1 DS tablet orally every 12 hours for 5 days. Alternatively, 8-10 mg TMP/kg/day intravenously divided every 6-12 hours can be administered for up to 5 days. 4. For traveler’s diarrhea caused by susceptible strains of enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli, the recommended dose is 1 DS tablet orally every 12 hours for 5 days. 5. For urinary tract infections (UTIs) caused by susceptible strains of Escherichia coli, Klebsiella species, Enterobacter species, Morganella morganii, Proteus mirabilis, and Proteus vulgaris, the recommended dose for pyelonephritis is 1 DS tablet or 2 regular-strength tablets orally every 12 hours for 14 days. For prostatitis, the dose is 1 DS tablet or 2 regular-strength tablets orally every 12 hours for 14 days or 2-3 months for chronic infections. For acute, uncomplicated cystitis, a 3-5 day course may be used. 6. For prophylaxis (off-label), various regimens exist, including using a regular-strength tablet once or twice per week, 1 DS tablet or 1 regular-strength tablet orally daily, or every 12 hours for up to 18 weeks. 7. Trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole is contraindicated in patients under 2 months of age. 8. For acute otitis media in pediatric patients caused by susceptible strains of Streptococcus pneumoniae or Haemophilus influenzae, the recommended dose for patients over 2 months of age is 6-10 mg TMP/kg/day orally divided every 12 hours for 10 days. It is contraindicated in patients under 2 months of age. 9. For beta-hemolytic Streptococcus infections, 8-12 mg TMP/kg/day orally divided every 12 hours for 5-10 days is recommended. A beta-lactam antibiotic should be added to the regimen if beta-hemolytic Streptococcus is suspected. 10. Aminobenzoate potassium decreases the effects of sulfamethoxazole through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 11. Aminolevulinic acid (oral or topical) increases the toxicity of sulfamethoxazole through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid administering other phototoxic drugs with aminolevulinic acid during the perioperative period. 12. Amiodarone and sulfamethoxazole or trimethoprim both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 13. Sulfamethoxazole increases the effects of antithrombin alfa by decreasing metabolism and through plasma protein binding competition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 14. Trimethoprim decreases the effects of live BCG vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Wait until antibiotic treatment is complete before administering live bacterial vaccines. 15. Apalutamide decreases the level or effect of trimethoprim by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Evaluate for loss of therapeutic effect if coadministration is necessary. 16. Sulfamethoxazole increases the effects of antithrombin III, argatroban, bemiparin, bivalirudin, dalteparin, enoxaparin, fondaparinux, and heparin by decreasing metabolism and through plasma protein binding competition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 17. Trimethoprim and sulfamethoxazole both increase the QTc interval when coadministered with disopyramide, ibutilide, pentamidine, pimozide, procainamide, quinidine, or sotalol. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 18. Trimethoprim increases the level or effect of erdafitinib, etrasimod, siponimod, and tucatinib by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 or CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Monitor for adverse reactions and adjust doses as needed if coadministration is unavoidable. 19. Sulfamethoxazole increases the effects of methotrexate by plasma protein binding competition, potentially elevating methotrexate concentrations and increasing the risk of toxicity (e.g., bone marrow suppression). Avoid or use an alternative drug. 20. Trimethoprim decreases the effects of microbiota oral therapy through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Complete antibiotic regimens 2-4 days before initiating microbiota oral therapy. 21. Sulfamethoxazole and pretomanid both increase the risk of hepatotoxicity. Avoid alcohol and hepatotoxic agents during pretomanid therapy. 22. Sulfamethoxazole and tretinoin (oral or topical) increase phototoxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 23. Trimethoprim increases the level or effect of tovrafenib by decreasing metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 24. Trilaciclib decreases the level or effect of trimethoprim by inhibiting OCT2, MATE1, and MATE-2K transporters. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Methenamine and sulfamethoxazole are contraindicated due to the potential formation of an insoluble precipitate in the urine, reducing the effects of both agents. 26. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of trimethoprim and sulfamethoxazole by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 27. Leucovorin and levoleucovorin decrease the effects of trimethoprim through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Monitor for treatment failure or decreased efficacy, especially in HIV-positive patients receiving trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole for Pneumocystis jiroveci pneumonia. 28. Pexidartinib increases the risk of hepatotoxicity. Avoid coadministration with other hepatotoxic agents. 29. Fexinidazole increases the level or effect of trimethoprim by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 30. Lopinavir increases the level or effect of trimethoprim by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug.
